title: The Trumpet and the Tomb
english: A sacred and royal trumpet has gathered this spiritual assembly for us: a trumpet that Bethlehem filled and Zion tempered in fire, on which the Cross was the hammer and the Resurrection the anvil. I do not know how to tell its beauty, how to describe its light, how to make known the joy within it, how to recount the kingdom within it. With what hand shall I touch it?

With what words shall I greet a tomb that gives birth to life, a grave free of corruption that yet brings about incorruption, a bridal chamber that laid the bridegroom to sleep for three days, a bridal room that raised the bride incorrupt after the marriage? The guarded tomb declares him dead, and the quaking earth declares him God. For his body cries out that he is dead, but the miracle that he is God; the burial, that he is dead, the resurrection, that he is God; the tears of the women, that he is dead, and the words of the angels, that he is God. Joseph buried him as one dead, but he who was buried as a man…
translator_notes: σφῦρα is 'hammer' and ἄκμων 'anvil'; ἐπύρωσεν is 'tempered in fire', as metal is worked in a forge.

μνῆμα φθορᾶς μὲν ἐλεύθερον, ἀφθαρσίας δὲ πρόξενον: 'a grave free of corruption that yet brings about incorruption'. The μὲν is an editor's supplement (set in angle brackets in the edition) and is followed.
παστάδα τριήμερον τὸν νυμφίον κοιμήσασαν: the bridal chamber 'for three days' (τριήμερον) in which the bridegroom slept.
Νεκρὸν ... θεόν: one verb, βοᾷ ('cries out, declares'), governs the whole series, so each pair reads 'declares him dead ... declares him God'.
This section ends in mid-sentence (ἀλλ' ὁ κηδευθεὶς ὡς ἄνθρωπος); the English gives 'as a man' here, and the sentence continues at the start of the next section.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia ii in sanctum pascha (Khazarzar) u01 open
